title: Edmund and the Hollow Again
premise: Jonah Eastwick, a beast-speaker hiding a forbidden gift in the border town of Thornfell, discovers her name and tonight's date in a century-old book of prophecies — and that same night, a stranger named Edmund arrives carrying the last map of Vellharrow, a country that vanished from maps and memory a hundred years ago. The prophecy binds them together: only the two of them can find Vellharrow's hidden door before the long winter seals it forever, but opening it demands one of them stay behind as the price of the other's survival. As smugglers, prophecy-hunters, and the mountain itself close in, Jonah and Edmund fall in love while each secretly plans to be the one who stays. In the end Jonah chooses the door — and discovers that 'staying behind' in Vellharrow means becoming its keeper in a country that exists only between winters, so she and Edmund part at the threshold, bound to meet again every year when the frost opens the way.
about_author: Beatrix Eastwick is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping mountain passes across three continents before turning to fiction. She writes from a stone farmhouse full of old maps, and claims every story begins with a road that shouldn't exist.

chapters.title: The Date That Wasn't Hers
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. In her grandfather's locked bookshop, Jonah finds a prophecy book dated a century back that names tonight's date — and her. She dismisses it as a smuggler's trick, but her gift stirs: the shop cat speaks a warning she's never heard a beast give. Beat: dread disguised as ordinary life.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Tollgate
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. A man named Edmund arrives on the last coach before winter, carrying a map of Vellharrow — a country Jonah has never heard of and no map should show. When she touches the map, every animal within earshot goes silent. Beat: the ordinary world cracks open.

chapters.title: What the Ravens Knew First
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund explains he inherited the map and a debt: his family were Vellharrow's cartographers, sworn to keep its door findable. He needs a guide through the Thornfell passes, and the prophecy names Jonah. She refuses. Beat: reluctant alliance, mutual suspicion.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Toll
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah's smuggling partners learn what Edmund carries and want it sold to the prophecy-hunters in Lowmark. Jonah must choose: betray Edmund or betray her crew. She steals the map back and runs. Beat: first irreversible choice.

chapters.title: Up the Frozen Stair
chapters.summary: Both POVs alternating. The two flee into the high passes as the first true snow falls. Jonah's gift becomes a liability — beasts along the trail repeat fragments of the prophecy in voices not their own. Beat: intimacy forged under pressure.

chapters.title: The Inn That Remembers
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. They shelter at an inn that predates Vellharrow's vanishing; its oldest guest, half-mad, recognizes Edmund's surname and weeps. Jonah learns the country didn't fall — it was closed, on purpose, to save it. Beat: the stakes deepen from escape to inheritance.

chapters.title: Hunters on the Ridge
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Prophecy-hunters from Lowmark catch their trail. Edmund reveals the prophecy's cruel clause: the door opens for two and keeps one. He lies to Jonah about which one. Beat: love complicated by a secret.

chapters.title: A Beast-Speaker's Bargain
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Cornered, Jonah bargains with a mountain bear — the first time she's used her gift as leverage rather than hiding it. The bear's price: a truth freely given. She admits she read the prophecy's ending and hid it from Edmund. Beat: honesty as turning point.

chapters.title: The Map Rewrites Itself
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The map redraws its own roads as winter deepens — Vellharrow is choosing them as much as they choose it. Edmund realizes his family's 'debt' was never to keep the door findable but to keep it shut. Beat: inheritance revealed as burden, not honor.

chapters.title: Lowmark's Auction
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Captured by the hunters, they're dragged to Lowmark where collectors bid on prophecy fragments. Jonah sees what the door is worth to people who'd burn a country to own it. Beat: clarity about what must never be sold.

chapters.title: The Escape Through the Bell-Tower
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. A desperate escape using Edmund's cartographic memory and Jonah's beasts — rats, pigeons, one furious goose. First time they fight as a unit instead of as strangers. Beat: trust made physical, joy inside danger.

chapters.title: What Jonah Hid
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah confesses the prophecy's ending: the keeper of the door cannot leave. She's known since chapter one. Edmund's fury and her shame give way to a harder truth — he'd already decided to stay and lied first. Beat: the secret's price paid in full.

chapters.title: Both Liars, One Road
chapters.summary: Both POVs. They almost part ways; the mountain forces them together through a whiteout. Stripped of secrets, they speak plainly about love and duty for the first time. Beat: quiet eye of the storm.

chapters.title: The Hollow Again
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. They reach the Hollow — a valley on no map where the vanished country bleeds through: ghost orchards, warm wind, a road that goes somewhere. The hunters regroup behind them. Beat: wonder and pursuit converging.

chapters.title: The Door in the Orchard
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The door is found — a gate in a blooming orchard under falling snow. But it will only open once, tonight, and the hunters arrive with fire. Beat: everything narrows to a single threshold.

chapters.title: Fire in the Ghost Orchard
chapters.summary: Both POVs. The hunters attack; Jonah calls every creature in the valley to defend the door. The battle is won at cost — the map burns, the orchard burns, the way in begins closing. Beat: climax of violence, sacrifice made real.

chapters.title: The Price Named Twice
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Both try to sacrifice themselves for the other, shoving and arguing at the threshold as the door narrows. The hunters' leader, dying, warns that a keeper who resents her door becomes its prisoner. Beat: climax of choice — love must be given, not traded.

chapters.title: Keeper
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah steps through willingly — not as payment but as answer, because Vellharrow is a country of beasts with no one to hear them, and she is a beast-speaker. The door seals behind her. Beat: duty and love reconciled, grief and rightness at once.

chapters.title: The Country Between Winters
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Inside, Jonah finds Vellharrow alive: people who chose to stay a century ago, beasts who sing her name. Edmund's map, half-burned, fell through with her — a thread. Beat: grief transformed into belonging.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Vigil
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Outside, Edmund survives the winter, rebuilds his family's work, and maps the Hollow's rhythms — discovering the door reopens every year at first frost. Beat: devotion as vocation; the long wait given shape.

chapters.title: First Frost, First Door
chapters.summary: Both POVs. A year later the gate opens. Edmund steps into Vellharrow carrying fresh maps and an offer: the door can hold two keepers if both are willing. Jonah has kept his half of the map warm all year. Beat: love against duty, resolved — the duty shared.

chapters.title: Edmund and the Hollow Again
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV, coda. The two keepers open the door each winter for those who need a country that doesn't exist, and close it each spring. The prophecy's last line, newly legible, simply reads: 'and the door remembered them kindly.' Beat: quiet, earned peace — inheritance turned into gift.
